question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

His father was killed in a ______, when the boy was nine years old.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. duel.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "duel" is a prearranged fight between two people with weapons (swords or pistols), fought according to fixed rules to settle a point of honour. (द्वंद्वयुद्ध)

◦ Correct: His father was killed in a duel, when the boy was nine years old.

• Only a fight can "kill" someone, so the noun required here is duel.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "dwell" is a verb meaning to live/reside somewhere; it cannot follow the article "a".

• Option 2 "drool" means to let saliva fall from the mouth — meaningless here.

• Option 3 "dual" is an adjective meaning double/having two parts (dual citizenship, dual control); an adjective cannot be the object of "in a ______".

NOTE

• Beware the classic homophone pair: duel (a fight — noun) vs dual (double — adjective). Similar SSC pairs: council/counsel, principal/principle, stationary/stationery, complement/compliment.

question:
Choose the word that can substitute the given group of words.

Something that is necessary or crucial
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Indispensable.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Indispensable" means absolutely necessary; essential; something that cannot be done without. (अनिवार्य / अपरिहार्य)

◦ Example: Water is indispensable to life.

• The prefix "in-" (not) + "dispensable" (that can be done away with) literally gives "that cannot be dispensed with".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Pedantic" — excessively concerned with minor rules and bookish details.

• Option 2 "Trivial" — of little value or importance; this is the opposite of the required meaning.

• Option 4 "Auxiliary" — giving additional or supporting help; extra, not essential.

NOTE

• Synonyms of indispensable: essential, vital, crucial, imperative, requisite. Antonyms: dispensable, unnecessary, superfluous, trivial.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Each band is known across a wide area because all residents of a given region are typically tied to one another through a large ______ of kinship and reciprocity
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. network.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "network" means a large interconnected system/group of people or things linked to one another. People "tied to one another" through kinship (family ties) and reciprocity (mutual give-and-take) form a network of relationships. (जाल / संजाल)

◦ Correct: ... all residents ... are typically tied to one another through a large network of kinship and reciprocity.

• The collocation "a network of" (a network of roads, a network of friends, a social network) is the standard English expression here.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "variation" (a change or difference in condition) does not describe ties between people.

• Option 2 "mesh" refers literally to netting/woven material; "a mesh of kinship" is not idiomatic English.

• Option 4 "clash" (a conflict or violent confrontation) contradicts "tied to one another", which is positive.

NOTE

• Useful collocations for SSC: a network of relations, a chain of events, a web of lies, a circle of friends, a flock of birds.

question:
Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'

The police released a statement saying/, "This was one of the most vicious/ attack we have ever seen."
option_2: The police released a statement saying,
option_3: "This was one of the most vicious
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. attack we have ever seen."

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The structure "one of the + superlative + plural noun" always takes a plural noun. So "one of the most vicious attacks", not "attack".

◦ Correct: The police released a statement saying, "This was one of the most vicious attacks we have ever seen."

• "One of ..." implies selecting one item out of a group, and a group must be plural.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "The police released a statement saying," is correct — "police" is a plural collective noun and takes a plural verb, and "released" is correctly in the past tense.

• '"This was one of the most vicious' is correct — "most vicious" is the proper superlative of the long adjective "vicious".

• Since a definite error exists, "No error" (Option 1) is wrong.

NOTE

• Remember the pattern: One of the + superlative + plural noun + singular verb — "One of the tallest buildings in the city is ...". Only the verb is singular; the noun after "one of the" must be plural.

question:
Select the appropriate antonym for the underlined word.

Social justice has been one of the cherished goals of the makers of our Constitution.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. despised.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Cherished" means held dear; deeply loved, valued and protected. (संजोया हुआ / प्रिय)

• Its antonym is "despised", meaning hated, looked down upon with contempt. (घृणा करना)

◦ Example: He cherished his mother's letters, but despised the man who wrote against her.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "relished" (enjoyed greatly) is close in sense to cherished — not an antonym.

• Option 2 "valued" (regarded as important) is a synonym of cherished.

• Option 3 "treasured" (kept as precious) is also a synonym.

NOTE

• Synonyms of cherish: treasure, value, prize, adore, hold dear, nurture. Antonyms: despise, loathe, abhor, detest, scorn, disdain.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the bracketed segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'no substitution required'.

This looks (like one of those unwelcome social summons which call upon a man) either to be bored or to lie.
option_1: like one of those unwelcome social summonses which call upon a man
option_2: like one of these unwelcome social summons that call upon a man
option_3: like one of those unwelcome social summon that call upon a man
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. like one of those unwelcome social summonses which call upon a man.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• After "one of those", the noun must be in the plural. The plural of the noun "summons" is "summonses" (summons – summonses), exactly like bus – buses, gas – gases.

◦ Correct: This looks like one of those unwelcome social summonses which call upon a man either to be bored or to lie.

• The relative pronoun "which" correctly refers back to the plural noun "summonses", and the plural verb "call" agrees with it.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 uses "these", which points to something near/at hand and clashes with the general, distant reference required here; it also keeps the wrong singular "summons".

• Option 3 uses "summon", which is a verb (to call/order someone to come), not the plural noun.

• Option 4 "No substitution required" is wrong because the singular "summons" after "one of those" is a clear grammatical error.

NOTE

• "Summons" (noun) = an official order to appear, especially in a court of law; plural summonses. "Summon" (verb) = to call someone to come or to order someone's presence. Nouns ending in -s, -ss, -sh, -ch, -x, -z form the plural by adding -es.

question:
Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose 'No improvement' as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct.

When I was eight years old, I used to played with toys.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. used to play.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The structure "used to + V1 (base form)" expresses a past habit or a repeated action that no longer happens. Hence "used to play", never "used to played".

◦ Correct: When I was eight years old, I used to play with toys.

• The time reference "When I was eight years old" clearly signals a discontinued past habit — the perfect context for "used to".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "No improvement" is wrong because "used to played" (to + V2) is ungrammatical.

• Option 2 "use to played" is doubly wrong — wrong tense form of "use" and wrong verb form after it.

• Option 3 "used to playing" would be right only in the different structure "be/get used to + V-ing" (= be accustomed to), e.g., "I am used to playing".

NOTE

• Distinguish carefully:

◦ used to + V1 = past habit ("I used to smoke").

◦ be used to + V-ing/noun = be accustomed to ("I am used to smoking / to the noise").

◦ get used to + V-ing = become accustomed to.

question:
Choose the word that means the same as the given word.

Wage
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Emolument.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Wage" (noun) means the money paid to a worker, usually for work done on an hourly, daily or weekly basis. (मज़दूरी / वेतन)

• "Emolument" means the salary, fee or profit received from employment or an office — the closest synonym. (उपलब्धि / पारिश्रमिक)

◦ Example: The judges' emoluments are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Sycophant" — a flatterer who praises powerful people for personal gain. (चापलूस)

• Option 2 "Jocular" — fond of joking, humorous. (विनोदी)

• Option 4 "Jackpot" — a large cash prize won in a game or lottery, not regular earned pay.

NOTE

• Synonyms of wage: salary, pay, earnings, remuneration, stipend, emolument, honorarium. Note also that "wage" as a verb means to carry on (a war/campaign) — "to wage war".

question:
Select the appropriate synonym for the underlined word.

There is no need to panic, not yet.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. fright.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Panic" means sudden uncontrollable fear or alarm that prevents clear thinking. (घबराहट / आतंक)

• "Fright" means sudden intense fear — the closest synonym among the options. (भय / डर)

◦ Example: The crowd was seized with panic/fright when the fire alarm rang.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "mock" — to make fun of, to ridicule.

• Option 2 "cheer" — to shout in joy or encouragement; this is the opposite in feeling.

• Option 4 "block" — to obstruct or stop something.

NOTE

• Synonyms of panic: fright, terror, alarm, dread, hysteria, consternation. Antonyms: calm, composure, serenity, confidence. Related idiom: "to press the panic button" = to react in a hurried, alarmed way.

question: Choose the incorrectly spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Monitour.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Monitour" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "Monitor" — a person or device that watches, checks or keeps track of something (also the display screen of a computer). (निगरानी करना / मॉनिटर)

◦ Spelling key: MO + NI + TOR (it ends in -tor, like actor, doctor, editor, inspector — not in "-tour").

◦ Correct: The nurse will monitor the patient's temperature every hour.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "Slope" (a surface with one end higher than the other), "Constant" (unchanging; continuous) and "Chemical" (relating to chemistry / a substance) are all spelt correctly.

NOTE

• Agent nouns from Latin usually end in -or: monitor, doctor, actor, sailor, governor, inspector, supervisor. Do not confuse with "tour" (a journey), which is a different word altogether.

question:
A sentence has been given with a blank to be filled with an appropriate option. Choose the correct alternative.

Potato milk is ______ another option for those wanting an alternative to cow's milk.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. yet.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Here "yet" is used as an adverb of emphasis before "another", giving the sense of "still one more / in addition to the ones already existing".

◦ Correct: Potato milk is yet another option for those wanting an alternative to cow's milk.

• "Yet another" is a fixed, idiomatic collocation meaning "one more of the same kind, added to many".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "though" and Option 4 "but" are contrast conjunctions; there is no contrast in this sentence, and neither can stand between "is" and "another".

• Option 3 "so" shows result/consequence, which the sentence does not express.

NOTE

• Other emphatic uses of "yet": "yet again" (once more), "yet more" (still more), "as yet" (up to now), "yet to come" (still in the future).

question:
In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom/Phrase.

To make one's mouth water
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Feel hungry.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "to make one's mouth water" means to make someone feel hungry / to create a strong desire for food by its sight or smell (because the mouth literally produces saliva). (मुँह में पानी आना)

◦ Example: The smell of hot samosas made my mouth water.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "To make faces" = to twist one's face into funny or rude expressions.

• Option 2 "To tremble with fear" corresponds to idioms like "to have one's heart in one's mouth" or "to shake like a leaf".

• Option 3 "To feel no pain" is unrelated to appetite.

NOTE

• Related food idioms: "mouth-watering" (delicious-looking), "eat like a horse" (eat a lot), "a piece of cake" (very easy), "bread and butter" (a means of livelihood).

question:
Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word.

Misunderstand
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Comprehend.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Misunderstand" means to fail to understand correctly; to interpret wrongly. (गलत समझना)

• Its antonym is "comprehend", meaning to grasp or understand fully. (समझना)

◦ Example: She did not misunderstand him; she comprehended his point perfectly.

• The prefix "mis-" means wrongly/badly: mis + understand = understand wrongly.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Impossible" (not able to happen) is unrelated to understanding.

• Option 3 "Delayed" (postponed, late) refers to time, not comprehension.

• Option 4 "Sluggish" (slow-moving, lacking energy) refers to speed/energy.

NOTE

• Words with the prefix mis- (wrongly): misjudge, misinterpret, mislead, misplace, misuse, misbehave. Synonyms of comprehend: understand, grasp, perceive, fathom, discern.

question:
Choose the word that can substitute the given group of words.

A sound that cannot be heard
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Inaudible.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Inaudible" means that cannot be heard (too faint for the ear to catch). (अश्रव्य)

◦ Formation: in- (not) + audible (able to be heard, from Latin "audire" = to hear).

◦ Example: His reply was almost inaudible over the noise of the traffic.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Audacious" — daring, bold, showing a willingness to take risks.

• Option 3 "Autonomous" — self-governing, independent.

• Option 4 "Delible" — that can be erased or rubbed out (its opposite, "indelible", means permanent).

NOTE

• Related one-word substitutes for SSC: invisible (that cannot be seen), illegible (that cannot be read), incorrigible (that cannot be corrected), inevitable (that cannot be avoided), edible (fit to be eaten), indelible (that cannot be erased).

question: Choose the sentence with no spelling error.
option_1: And he wanted to sea him sufer.
option_2: And he wanted to see him sufer.
option_3: And he wanted to see him suffer.
option_4: And he wantted to see him suffer.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. And he wanted to see him suffer.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• All three words are correctly spelt only in Option 3:

◦ "wanted" — WANT + ED (single "t"),

◦ "see" — to perceive with the eyes,

◦ "suffer" — to undergo pain or hardship, spelt with a double "f" (SUF + FER).

◦ Correct: And he wanted to see him suffer.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 has two errors — "sea" (a large body of salt water, a homophone of "see") and "sufer" (missing an "f").

• Option 2 misspells "suffer" as "sufer".

• Option 4 misspells "wanted" as "wantted" (the final "t" is not doubled because the stress and vowel pattern do not require it).

NOTE

• Doubling rule: a final consonant is doubled before -ed/-ing only in a stressed syllable with a single short vowel — stop → stopped, plan → planned. "Want" ends in -nt (two consonants), so it stays single: wanted.

question:
Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose 'No improvement' as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct.

After the concert, his voice has hoarse from cheering.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. voice was.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Hoarse" is an adjective (rough and harsh in sound), so it needs a linking verb (be), not the auxiliary "has". Since the event is over — "After the concert" — the simple past "was" is required.

◦ Correct: After the concert, his voice was hoarse from cheering.

• "voice" is a singular subject, so the singular past form "was" agrees with it.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "No improvement" is wrong because "his voice has hoarse" has no main verb linking the adjective.

• Option 3 "voiced was" wrongly turns the noun "voice" into a verb, leaving the sentence without a subject.

• Option 4 "voice were" breaks subject–verb agreement — a singular subject cannot take "were".

NOTE

• Note the homophones: hoarse (rough-voiced) and horse (the animal). Linking verbs (be, seem, appear, become, feel, look, sound) are followed by adjectives, not adverbs — "His voice was hoarse", "She looks tired".

question:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error'.

Why is your friend giving me weird looks?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. No error.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence is completely correct, so "No error" is the right choice.

◦ "Why is your friend" — correct interrogative word order: question word (Why) + auxiliary (is) + subject (your friend).

◦ "giving me" — correct present-continuous form ("is giving") with the indirect object "me".

◦ "weird looks?" — "weird" (strange, odd) is correctly spelt and correctly modifies the plural noun "looks"; the question mark is properly placed.

• Full sentence: Why is your friend giving me weird looks?

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• The present continuous ("is giving") is appropriate because the action is happening at the moment of speaking.

• "Give someone a look / looks" is a standard collocation meaning to look at someone in a particular way.

NOTE

• Spelling tip: "weird" is a famous exception to the "i before e except after c" rule — remember "we are weird". Question-formation rule: Wh-word + auxiliary + subject + main verb.

question:
A sentence has been given with a blank to be filled with an appropriate option. Choose the correct alternative.

She had no ______ of telling him the truth.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. intention.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• After the determiner "no", a noun is needed, and the correct noun form is "intention" (a plan or aim to do something). (इरादा / मंशा)

◦ Correct: She had no intention of telling him the truth.

• The fixed structure is "to have no intention of + V-ing" — note the preposition "of" followed by the gerund "telling".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "intending" is a present participle/gerund, not the noun required after "no".

• Option 2 "intended" is a past participle/adjective ("the intended result").

• Option 3 "intents" is used only in the fixed legal phrase "to all intents and purposes"; "no intents of" is not idiomatic.

NOTE

• Word family: intend (verb), intention (noun), intentional (adjective), intentionally (adverb). Compare structures: "intend to do" but "have no intention of doing".

question:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error'.

Soap removes traces of pesticides and heavy metals that hand sanitizers can left behind.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. sanitizers can left behind.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• After a modal verb such as "can", the verb must be in its base form (V1). Hence it should be "can leave behind", not "can left behind".

◦ Correct: Soap removes traces of pesticides and heavy metals that hand sanitizers can leave behind.

• "left" is the past/past-participle form (leave – left – left) and cannot follow "can".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "Soap removes traces of pesticides" is correct — "soap" is an uncountable singular subject taking the singular verb "removes".

• "and heavy metals that hand" is correct — the relative pronoun "that" properly introduces the clause describing the traces.

• As a clear error exists, "No error" (Option 4) is wrong.

NOTE

• Modals (can, could, may, might, shall, should, will, would, must) are always followed by the bare infinitive (V1): "He can swim", "She must go", "They should have gone" (have + V3, never "must went").

question:
In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom/Phrase.

To turn over a new leaf
option_1: To have an inclination towards gardening
option_3: To turn your back on someone
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. To make a fresh start.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "to turn over a new leaf" means to change one's behaviour for the better; to make a completely fresh start. Here "leaf" means a page of a book — turning it over begins a clean, blank page. (नया जीवन शुरू करना / सुधर जाना)

◦ Example: After his release from jail, he decided to turn over a new leaf and start an honest business.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 takes "leaf" literally as a plant leaf — a trap answer.

• Option 3 "To turn your back on someone" is a different idiom meaning to abandon or refuse to help someone.

• Option 4 "To reply brazenly" corresponds to "to answer back" or "to be barefaced", not to this idiom.

NOTE

• Related idioms of change and beginning: "start afresh / from scratch", "wipe the slate clean", "a clean slate", "mend one's ways".

question:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

To mark the 25th anniversary of the run, (1) ______ Royal Canadian Mint unveiled a one-dollar commemorative circulation coin (2) ______ Monday on the campus of Simon Fraser University. Fox was (3) ______ undergraduate student and basketball player at SFU when a malignant tumour was discovered in his right leg in 1977. It resulted in (4) ______. A bronze statue of Fox, one of many such tributes across Canada, looks over the academic quadrangle of the university, just a short stroll from the theatre where Monday's (5) ______ was held.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank No. 1
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. the.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Royal Canadian Mint" is the name of a unique, one-of-its-kind institution, and names of such specific bodies take the definite article "the".

◦ Correct: ... (1) the Royal Canadian Mint unveiled a one-dollar commemorative circulation coin ...

• Rule: "the" is used before the names of organisations, departments, and institutions of the pattern "the + Adjective + Noun" (the Reserve Bank of India, the United Nations, the Supreme Court).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "a" is the indefinite article used for a non-specific, first-mentioned singular countable noun — wrong for a unique named institution.

• Options 2 "in" and 3 "of" are prepositions; the blank is followed by a noun phrase acting as the subject of "unveiled", so a preposition cannot fit.

NOTE

• "The" is used with: unique objects (the sun, the moon), rivers/oceans/mountain ranges (the Ganga, the Himalayas), newspapers (the Hindu), organisations (the WHO), and superlatives (the best).

question:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

To mark the 25th anniversary of the run, (1) ______ Royal Canadian Mint unveiled a one-dollar commemorative circulation coin (2) ______ Monday on the campus of Simon Fraser University. Fox was (3) ______ undergraduate student and basketball player at SFU when a malignant tumour was discovered in his right leg in 1977. It resulted in (4) ______. A bronze statue of Fox, one of many such tributes across Canada, looks over the academic quadrangle of the university, just a short stroll from the theatre where Monday's (5) ______ was held.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank No. 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. on.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The preposition "on" is used before the days of the week and before specific dates. The blank is followed by "Monday", so "on Monday" is required.

◦ Correct: ... unveiled a one-dollar commemorative circulation coin (2) on Monday on the campus of Simon Fraser University.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "at" is used for exact points of clock time and for specific places (at 5 o'clock, at night, at the door) — not with days.

• Option 2 "through" indicates movement from one end to another or duration ("through the tunnel", "Monday through Friday").

• Option 4 "over" means above or across, or during an extended period ("over the weekend") — not with a single named day.

NOTE

• Prepositions of time: at + clock time (at 6 pm, at noon, at night); on + days/dates (on Monday, on 15 August); in + months/years/seasons/parts of the day (in July, in 2023, in winter, in the morning).

question:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

To mark the 25th anniversary of the run, (1) ______ Royal Canadian Mint unveiled a one-dollar commemorative circulation coin (2) ______ Monday on the campus of Simon Fraser University. Fox was (3) ______ undergraduate student and basketball player at SFU when a malignant tumour was discovered in his right leg in 1977. It resulted in (4) ______. A bronze statue of Fox, one of many such tributes across Canada, looks over the academic quadrangle of the university, just a short stroll from the theatre where Monday's (5) ______ was held.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank No. 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. an.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank is followed by "undergraduate", which begins with the vowel sound /ʌ/. Before a vowel sound, the indefinite article "an" is used.

◦ Correct: Fox was (3) an undergraduate student and basketball player at SFU ...

• Also, this is the first mention of Fox's status, so an indefinite article (a/an) is right, not "the".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "their" is a plural possessive and cannot refer to the singular "Fox".

• Option 2 "a" is used only before a consonant sound; "a undergraduate" is wrong.

• Option 4 "the" would wrongly suggest a particular, already-known student.

NOTE

• The a/an choice depends on sound, not spelling: an hour, an honest man, an MP, an X-ray (vowel sounds) vs a university, a European, a one-rupee coin, a useful book (consonant /j/ and /w/ sounds).

question:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

To mark the 25th anniversary of the run, (1) ______ Royal Canadian Mint unveiled a one-dollar commemorative circulation coin (2) ______ Monday on the campus of Simon Fraser University. Fox was (3) ______ undergraduate student and basketball player at SFU when a malignant tumour was discovered in his right leg in 1977. It resulted in (4) ______. A bronze statue of Fox, one of many such tributes across Canada, looks over the academic quadrangle of the university, just a short stroll from the theatre where Monday's (5) ______ was held.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank No. 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. amputation.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Amputation" means the surgical removal (cutting off) of a limb or part of the body. A malignant tumour discovered in his right leg would medically "result in" the amputation of that leg. (अंगच्छेदन)

◦ Correct: ... when a malignant tumour was discovered in his right leg in 1977. It resulted in (4) amputation.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "fragmentation" — breaking into small pieces or parts; not a surgical treatment for a leg tumour.

• Option 3 "vasodilation" — the widening of blood vessels; unrelated to a tumour of the bone.

• Option 4 "implantation" — the insertion of tissue or a device into the body — the opposite of removal.

NOTE

• The passage refers to Terry Fox, the Canadian athlete whose right leg was amputated because of osteosarcoma; he then began the "Marathon of Hope" run across Canada to raise money for cancer research, and is commemorated by statues and by a Royal Canadian Mint coin.

question:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

To mark the 25th anniversary of the run, (1) ______ Royal Canadian Mint unveiled a one-dollar commemorative circulation coin (2) ______ Monday on the campus of Simon Fraser University. Fox was (3) ______ undergraduate student and basketball player at SFU when a malignant tumour was discovered in his right leg in 1977. It resulted in (4) ______. A bronze statue of Fox, one of many such tributes across Canada, looks over the academic quadrangle of the university, just a short stroll from the theatre where Monday's (5) ______ was held.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank No. 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. unveiling.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Unveiling" (noun) means a ceremony at which something new — a coin, a statue, a plaque — is formally shown to the public for the first time. (अनावरण)

• The passage itself says the Mint "unveiled" the coin, so the event held in the theatre was the unveiling.

◦ Correct: ... just a short stroll from the theatre where Monday's (5) unveiling was held.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "countervailing" — acting against something with equal force (as in "countervailing duty" in trade).

• Option 3 "reconciling" — bringing into agreement or making friendly again.

• Option 4 "veiling" — covering or concealing, the exact opposite of unveiling.

NOTE

• Word family: veil (a covering) → unveil (to remove the cover, to reveal) → unveiling (the ceremony of revealing). Similar pairs: cover/uncover, mask/unmask, cover-up/disclosure.

question: Which acid destroys the bacteria that enter the stomach?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Hydrochloric acid.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Hydrochloric acid (HCl)" is secreted by the parietal (oxyntic) cells of the gastric glands in the stomach. It makes the stomach strongly acidic (pH about 1.5–3.5), which kills the bacteria and germs that enter with food. (हाइड्रोक्लोरिक अम्ल — जठर रस)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• HCl also converts the inactive enzyme pepsinogen into active pepsin, which digests proteins.

• The stomach lining is protected from this acid by a layer of mucus; when this protection fails, peptic ulcers occur.

• Excess acid causes acidity/hyperacidity, treated with antacids (mild bases such as magnesium hydroxide — milk of magnesia).

NOTE

• Other options: Nitric acid (HNO₃) — a strong industrial acid; Boric acid (H₃BO₃) — a weak antiseptic used externally; Uric acid — a waste product excreted in urine, whose excess causes gout.

question: Which among the following wind is associated with extreme cold and dryness?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Polar Easterlies.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Polar Easterlies" are the cold, dry prevailing winds that blow from the high-pressure polar regions (about 90°) towards the sub-polar low-pressure belts (about 60°) in both hemispheres. Because they originate over the ice-covered poles, they are extremely cold and dry. (ध्रुवीय पुरवा हवाएँ)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Trade Winds blow from the sub-tropical high (30°) towards the equatorial low; they are warm and, over oceans, moisture-laden.

• Westerlies blow from the sub-tropical high (30°) towards the sub-polar low (60°); in the Southern Hemisphere they are called the Roaring Forties, Furious Fifties and Shrieking Sixties.

• Monsoon winds are seasonal winds that reverse direction between summer and winter, bringing rain to South Asia.

NOTE

• All permanent winds are deflected by the Coriolis force — to the right in the Northern Hemisphere and to the left in the Southern Hemisphere (Ferrel's law).

question: Baisakhi Festival is majorly celebrated in the states of ______ and ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Punjab, Haryana.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Baisakhi (Vaisakhi)" is celebrated mainly in Punjab and Haryana. It marks the harvest of the rabi crop and the Sikh New Year, and is observed around 13/14 April. (बैसाखी — पंजाब और हरियाणा)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Historically, on Baisakhi in 1699, Guru Gobind Singh (the tenth Sikh Guru) founded the Khalsa Panth at Anandpur Sahib.

• The Jallianwala Bagh massacre at Amritsar also took place on Baisakhi day, 13 April 1919.

• Celebrations include the Bhangra and Gidda folk dances and processions (Nagar Kirtan) from gurudwaras.

NOTE

• The same day is celebrated under different names: Bihu (Assam), Poila Boishakh (West Bengal), Puthandu (Tamil Nadu), Vishu (Kerala), Pana Sankranti (Odisha) and Jur Sital (Bihar).

question:
Cash reserve ratio is a ________ tool to control money supply.

I. Qualitative

II. Quantitative
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only II.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) is a quantitative (general) credit-control tool of the Reserve Bank of India. It is the percentage of a bank's Net Demand and Time Liabilities (NDTL) that must be kept with the RBI as cash. (नकद आरक्षित अनुपात — मात्रात्मक उपकरण)

• Raising the CRR reduces lendable funds and contracts money supply; lowering it expands money supply. Hence only statement II (Quantitative) is correct.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Quantitative tools: Bank Rate, Repo Rate, Reverse Repo Rate, CRR, SLR, Open Market Operations (OMO), Marginal Standing Facility (MSF).

• Qualitative (selective) tools: margin requirements, moral suasion, credit rationing, direct action, regulation of consumer credit.

• No interest is paid by the RBI on CRR balances, whereas SLR is maintained by banks themselves in cash, gold or approved securities.

NOTE

• The RBI is India's central bank, established on 1 April 1935 under the RBI Act, 1934, and nationalised in 1949. Monetary policy is decided by the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC).

question: Which battle led to the destruction of the Vijayanagara empire?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Battle of Talikota.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Battle of Talikota (1565)" was fought between the Vijayanagara Empire and a confederacy of the Deccan Sultanates (Bijapur, Ahmadnagar, Golconda and Bidar). Vijayanagara was decisively defeated, its regent Aliya Rama Raya was killed, and the capital Hampi was sacked — leading to the empire's collapse. (तालीकोटा का युद्ध — 1565)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Battle of Raichur (1520) was won by Krishnadeva Raya of Vijayanagara against Bijapur.

• The Battle of Haldighati (1576) was fought between Maharana Pratap and Akbar's forces led by Man Singh.

• The Battle of Arcot (1751) was part of the Anglo-French Carnatic Wars, where Robert Clive made his name.

NOTE

• The Vijayanagara Empire was founded in 1336 by Harihara I and Bukka Raya I (Sangama dynasty); its greatest ruler was Krishnadeva Raya (Tuluva dynasty). Its ruins at Hampi are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

question: Mahabalipuram Monuments were built in ______ dynasty architecture.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pallava.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Group of Monuments at Mahabalipuram (Mamallapuram) in Tamil Nadu was built under the Pallava dynasty in the 7th–8th centuries CE, chiefly by Narasimhavarman I (Mamalla) and Narasimhavarman II (Rajasimha). (पल्लव वंश — महाबलीपुरम)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Famous structures there: the Shore Temple, the Pancha Rathas (five monolithic temples named after the Pandavas), the Varaha Cave Temple, and the great open-air relief "Descent of the Ganges / Arjuna's Penance".

• It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and represents the beginning of Dravidian temple architecture.

NOTE

• The Chandellas built the Khajuraho temples (Madhya Pradesh); the Guptas built the Dashavatara temple at Deogarh; "Pali" is an ancient language, not a dynasty.

question: V. Satyanarayana Sarma was awarded with Padma Shri in 1970 for his contributions in the field of ________ dance.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kuchipudi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Vedantam Satyanarayana Sarma was a legendary exponent of the Kuchipudi classical dance of Andhra Pradesh, celebrated especially for his portrayal of Satyabhama in "Bhama Kalapam". He received the Padma Shri in 1970. (कुचिपुड़ी — वेदांतम सत्यनारायण शर्मा)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Kuchipudi takes its name from the village Kuchelapuram in Andhra Pradesh; it was systematised by Siddhendra Yogi and combines dance, song and acting (its performers traditionally sing while they dance).

• A famous Kuchipudi item is the Tarangam, danced on the rim of a brass plate.

NOTE

• The eight classical dances of India: Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kathak (North India), Kathakali and Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur) and Sattriya (Assam).

question: In ______, at its Madras session, the Indian National Congress set up an All Parties Conference to draft a Constitution for India.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1927.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• At its Madras session of 1927 (presided over by Dr. M. A. Ansari), the Indian National Congress responded to the all-white Simon Commission by calling for an All Parties Conference to draft a Constitution for India. (1927 — मद्रास अधिवेशन)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The committee appointed by that conference was headed by Motilal Nehru, and its report — the Nehru Report (1928) — was the first major Indian attempt at framing a constitution. It demanded Dominion Status, fundamental rights and a federal structure.

• The Simon Commission (1927) was boycotted with the slogan "Simon Go Back"; Lala Lajpat Rai was fatally injured in a lathi charge during a protest at Lahore.

NOTE

• Key Congress sessions: 1885 Bombay (first, W. C. Bonnerjee), 1906 Calcutta (Swaraj demand, Dadabhai Naoroji), 1907 Surat (split), 1916 Lucknow (Congress–League Pact), 1929 Lahore (Purna Swaraj, Jawaharlal Nehru).

question: According to census 2011, which Union territory has highest decadal population growth rate between 2001 - 11?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dadra & Nagar Haveli.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per Census 2011, Dadra & Nagar Haveli recorded the highest decadal population growth rate (2001–2011) among the Union Territories — about 55.9%, driven mainly by heavy in-migration for industrial work. (दादरा और नगर हवेली — सर्वाधिक दशकीय वृद्धि दर)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Among states, Meghalaya had the highest decadal growth (27.9%) and Nagaland the lowest (–0.6%).

• India's overall decadal growth in 2001–11 was 17.7%; total population 1,210.9 million; density 382 persons per sq km; sex ratio 943; literacy 74.04%.

• Census 2011 was the 15th national census and the 7th since Independence, with the slogan "Our Census, Our Future".

NOTE

• In 2020, Dadra & Nagar Haveli was merged with Daman & Diu into a single Union Territory. Lakshadweep is India's least populous UT.

question: Koneru Humpy is associated with which of the following sport?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chess.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Koneru Humpy, from Andhra Pradesh, is one of India's greatest chess players. In 2002, at the age of 15, she became a Grandmaster — then the youngest woman ever to do so. (कोनेरू हम्पी — शतरंज)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• She won the Women's World Rapid Chess Championship in 2019 (and again in 2024) and has been awarded the Arjuna Award (2003), Padma Shri (2007) and the Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna (2020).

• Viswanathan Anand was India's first Grandmaster (1988) and a five-time World Chess Champion.

NOTE

• Chess is believed to have originated in India as "Chaturanga". The world governing body is FIDE, and 20 July is celebrated as International Chess Day.

question: Which among the following countries will host the 2024 South Asian Games?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pakistan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Pakistan was selected to host the 14th South Asian Games (2024), with Islamabad, Lahore and Faisalabad as the proposed venues. (दक्षिण एशियाई खेल 2024 — पाकिस्तान)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The South Asian Games (SAG) are a biennial multi-sport event of the South Asian Olympic Council (SAOC) for the eight SAARC nations — India, Pakistan, Nepal, Bhutan, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Maldives and Afghanistan.

• The first edition was held in Kathmandu, Nepal, in 1984.

• The 13th edition (2019) was hosted by Nepal (Kathmandu and Pokhara), where India topped the medal tally.

NOTE

• SAARC (South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation) was founded in 1985 at Dhaka, with its secretariat at Kathmandu.

question: Union Agriculture Minister Narendra Singh Tomar announced in October 2022 that the central government will launch a ______ crore accelerator programme to support the productive ideas of agro businesses.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rs.500.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In October 2022, the then Union Agriculture Minister Narendra Singh Tomar announced a Rs.500 crore agriculture accelerator programme/fund to support agri start-ups and agro-business ideas. (500 करोड़ रुपये का कृषि त्वरक कार्यक्रम)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Agriculture Accelerator Fund was subsequently announced in the Union Budget 2023-24 to encourage agri start-ups by young entrepreneurs in rural areas, bringing innovative and affordable solutions to farmers' challenges.

• Related schemes: PM-KISAN (Rs.6,000 per year to farmers), PMFBY (crop insurance), e-NAM (online national agriculture market) and the Agriculture Infrastructure Fund.

NOTE

• The Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare also runs the RKVY-RAFTAAR scheme, which funds agri-business incubation and start-ups.

question: 'India's Struggle for Independence' is one of the notable books written by ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bipan Chandra.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "India's Struggle for Independence (1857–1947)" was written by the eminent historian Bipan Chandra along with Mridula Mukherjee, Aditya Mukherjee, K. N. Panikkar and Sucheta Mahajan; it was published in 1988. (बिपन चंद्र)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Bipan Chandra's other works: The Rise and Growth of Economic Nationalism in India, Communalism in Modern India, Essays on Colonialism and India Since Independence.

• He was a Marxist-influenced nationalist historian and served as Chairman of the National Book Trust.

NOTE

• Other options: Sekhar Bandyopadhyay wrote "From Plassey to Partition"; R. C. Majumdar wrote "History of the Freedom Movement in India"; R. K. Narayan was a novelist ("Malgudi Days", "The Guide", "Swami and Friends").

question: The Inter-State Council consists of ______ ministers of Cabinet rank in the Union Council of Ministers nominated by the Prime Minister of India.
solution_text:
The correct answer is six.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Inter-State Council includes six ministers of Cabinet rank in the Union Council of Ministers, nominated by the Prime Minister, besides the Prime Minister (Chairman), the Chief Ministers of all States, the Chief Ministers of UTs with legislatures and the Administrators of other UTs. (अंतर्राज्यीय परिषद — छह कैबिनेट मंत्री)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Council is a constitutional body established under Article 263 of the Constitution by a Presidential Order in 1990, on the recommendation of the Sarkaria Commission.

• Its functions are to inquire into and advise on disputes between States, to investigate and discuss subjects of common interest, and to make recommendations for better policy coordination.

NOTE

• Related bodies: Zonal Councils (statutory, under the States Reorganisation Act, 1956), the Finance Commission (Article 280) and NITI Aayog (2015, which replaced the Planning Commission).

question: Fundamental Duties were incorporated in Part IV-A of the Constitution by the ______ Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976 on the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 42nd.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Fundamental Duties were added to the Constitution in Part IV-A (Article 51A) by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976, on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee. Originally ten duties were listed. (42वाँ संविधान संशोधन, 1976)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The 86th Amendment Act, 2002 added the 11th duty — that every parent/guardian should provide opportunities for education to their child (or ward) between the ages of 6 and 14 years.

• Fundamental Duties are borrowed from the Constitution of the erstwhile USSR and, like the Directive Principles, are non-justiciable (not enforceable by courts).

• The 42nd Amendment is called the "Mini-Constitution"; it also added the words Socialist, Secular and Integrity to the Preamble.

NOTE

• Article 51A duties include respecting the Constitution, the National Flag and the National Anthem, cherishing the ideals of the freedom struggle, protecting the environment, developing a scientific temper, and safeguarding public property.

question: Nepal does NOT share its boundary with which of the following states in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Manipur.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Nepal shares its border with five Indian states — Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, West Bengal and Sikkim. Manipur does NOT touch Nepal; it lies in the north-east and borders Myanmar. (मणिपुर — नेपाल से सीमा नहीं)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The India–Nepal border is about 1,751 km long and is an open border allowing free movement of citizens.

• Indian states bordering Myanmar: Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, Manipur and Mizoram.

• Indian states bordering Bhutan: Sikkim, West Bengal, Assam and Arunachal Pradesh.

NOTE

• Bangladesh shares the longest border with India (about 4,096 km), followed by China (about 3,488 km) and Pakistan (about 3,323 km). The Line of Actual Control (LAC) faces China and the Radcliffe Line faces Pakistan and Bangladesh.

question: "Mission Karmayogi" programme is for ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Civil servants.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Mission Karmayogi", launched in September 2020, is the National Programme for Civil Services Capacity Building (NPCSCB). It aims to make Indian civil servants more creative, proactive, professional, innovative and technology-enabled. (मिशन कर्मयोगी — सिविल सेवक)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• It seeks a shift from a rule-based to a role-based approach to human resource management, matching officials' competencies to their posts.

• Its online learning platform is iGOT-Karmayogi (Integrated Government Online Training).

• Its institutional framework includes the PM's Human Resource Council, a Capacity Building Commission and a Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV).

NOTE

• The word "Karmayogi" comes from the Bhagavad Gita, denoting one who performs duty selflessly. The programme is run by the Department of Personnel and Training (DoPT).

question: Who among the following was awarded the Bharat Ratna in 2001 and has been credited with taking the shehnai from the marriage mandap to the concert hall?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bismillah Khan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Ustad Bismillah Khan was awarded the Bharat Ratna in 2001. He is credited with raising the shehnai from a folk instrument played at weddings and temples to the status of a classical concert instrument. (उस्ताद बिस्मिल्लाह खान — शहनाई)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• He played the shehnai from the Red Fort on 15 August 1947, India's first Independence Day, and again on Republic Day 1950.

• He was closely associated with the Kashi Vishwanath temple, Varanasi, and received the Padma Shri, Padma Bhushan, Padma Vibhushan and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award.

NOTE

• Other musicians with the Bharat Ratna: M. S. Subbulakshmi (1998), Ravi Shankar (1999, sitar), Lata Mangeshkar (2001) and Bhupen Hazarika (2019, posthumous). Hariprasad Chaurasia plays the flute and Ali Akbar Khan played the sarod.

question: In 1895, Mahatma Gandhi, along with other Indians has established ______ to fight against racial discrimination.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Natal Congress.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In 1894–95, Mahatma Gandhi, together with other Indians in South Africa, founded the Natal Indian Congress (NIC) at Durban to organise the Indian community and to fight racial discrimination against Indians in Natal. (नेटाल इंडियन कांग्रेस — 1894/95)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Gandhi went to South Africa in 1893 as a lawyer for the firm of Dada Abdulla and developed his technique of Satyagraha (non-violent resistance) there.

• He also founded the Phoenix Settlement (1904) near Durban and the Tolstoy Farm (1910) near Johannesburg, and started the newspaper Indian Opinion (1903).

• He returned to India in 1915; 9 January is celebrated as Pravasi Bharatiya Divas to mark that return.

NOTE

• Other options: the Brahmo Samaj (1828) was founded by Raja Ram Mohan Roy; the Dev Samaj (1887) by Shiv Narayan Agnihotri at Lahore; the Sabarmati Ashram (1917) was set up by Gandhi at Ahmedabad.

question: Padma Subrahmanyam is a well-known dancer of which of the following dance forms?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bharatnatyam.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Dr. Padma Subrahmanyam is a celebrated Bharatanatyam dancer, choreographer, researcher and scholar from Tamil Nadu, known for reviving the "Karanas" described in Bharata Muni's Natya Shastra — a style she named Bharata Nrityam. (पद्मा सुब्रह्मण्यम — भरतनाट्यम)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• She has received the Padma Shri, Padma Bhushan, Padma Vibhushan (2024) and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award, and also Japan's Fukuoka Asian Culture Prize.

• Bharatanatyam is the classical dance of Tamil Nadu, once performed in temples as Sadir/Dasiattam, and revived in the 20th century by Rukmini Devi Arundale and E. Krishna Iyer.

NOTE

• Other famous Bharatanatyam exponents: Rukmini Devi Arundale, Yamini Krishnamurthy, Mallika Sarabhai, Sonal Mansingh and Vyjayanthimala.

question: Fern is an example of which plant group?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pteridophyta.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The fern belongs to the group Pteridophyta — plants that have a well-differentiated body (root, stem and leaves) and true vascular tissue (xylem and phloem) but bear no flowers or seeds; they reproduce by spores. (टेरिडोफाइटा — फर्न)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Other pteridophytes: Marsilea, Equisetum (horsetail) and Selaginella.

• Thallophyta (algae) have an undifferentiated thallus body; Bryophyta (mosses, Riccia, Marchantia) are the "amphibians of the plant kingdom" and lack vascular tissue.

• Phanerogams (spermatophytes) are seed-bearing plants, divided into Gymnosperms (naked seeds — pine, cycas) and Angiosperms (seeds in fruits).

NOTE

• Whittaker's five-kingdom classification (1969): Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae and Animalia. Plants without seeds (Thallophyta, Bryophyta, Pteridophyta) are together called Cryptogams.

question: The ambassador who was sent to the court of Chandragupta Maurya by the Greek ruler Seleucus Nicator is ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Megasthenes.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Megasthenes was the Greek ambassador sent by Seleucus Nicator to the court of Chandragupta Maurya at Pataliputra. He wrote the account "Indica", which describes Mauryan society, the city of Pataliputra and its administration. (मेगस्थनीज — इंडिका)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Chandragupta Maurya founded the Mauryan Empire in 322/321 BCE with the help of Chanakya (Kautilya), who wrote the Arthashastra.

• Chandragupta defeated Seleucus Nicator around 305 BCE; by the treaty he gained territories and gave Seleucus 500 war elephants.

• Later Greek envoys to the Mauryas were Deimachus (to Bindusara) and Dionysius (to Ashoka, sent by Ptolemy II).

NOTE

• Homer was the Greek epic poet (Iliad, Odyssey); Herodotus is called the "Father of History"; Strabo was a Greek geographer — none of them visited the Mauryan court.

question: Hindustan Aeronautics limited comes under which sector?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Public sector.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL) is a public sector undertaking (PSU) owned by the Government of India and administered by the Ministry of Defence. (हिंदुस्तान एयरोनॉटिक्स लिमिटेड — सार्वजनिक क्षेत्र)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• HAL is headquartered at Bengaluru; it began as Hindustan Aircraft Limited, founded by Walchand Hirachand in 1940, and became HAL in 1964.

• It manufactures the Tejas (LCA), the Dhruv advanced light helicopter, the HTT-40 trainer and the LCH Prachand, and it also assembles the Su-30MKI.

• HAL holds Maharatna status (conferred in 2024) among central public sector enterprises.

NOTE

• Public sector = owned and run by the government (HAL, BHEL, ONGC, SAIL, IOCL); private sector = owned by individuals/companies; co-operative sector = owned by members (AMUL, IFFCO).

question: Newton's first law of motion is also known as ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Law of Inertia.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Newton's First Law of Motion states that a body continues in its state of rest or of uniform motion in a straight line unless acted upon by an external unbalanced force. Because it defines the property of inertia, it is called the "Law of Inertia". (जड़त्व का नियम)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Inertia is the tendency of a body to resist any change in its state of rest or motion; its measure is the body's mass — greater mass means greater inertia.

• Newton's Second Law: F = ma; the rate of change of momentum is proportional to the applied force.

• Newton's Third Law: to every action there is an equal and opposite reaction.

NOTE

• Everyday examples of inertia: passengers lurch forward when a bus brakes suddenly (inertia of motion) and backward when it starts (inertia of rest); dust falls off a carpet when it is beaten. Newton stated these laws in the Principia Mathematica (1687).

question: Which river is the third largest in the peninsula of India and the largest river of Odisha state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mahanadi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Mahanadi is the third largest river of peninsular India (after the Godavari and the Krishna) and the largest river of Odisha. It rises near Sihawa in the Dhamtari district of Chhattisgarh and flows east into the Bay of Bengal, forming a large delta. (महानदी — ओडिशा)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Hirakud Dam on the Mahanadi (in Odisha) is one of the longest dams in the world and was among independent India's first major multipurpose river valley projects.

• Its main tributaries are the Seonath, Hasdeo, Mand, Ib, Jonk and Tel; Cuttack and Sambalpur lie on its banks.

NOTE

• Peninsular rivers flowing east into the Bay of Bengal: Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna, Kaveri (they form deltas). Rivers flowing west into the Arabian Sea: Narmada and Tapi (they flow through rift valleys and form estuaries).
